text: Earn the first €20 of compute through an accepted open-source bounty
description: Run the Compute Commons Maintainer experiment defined in meta/autonomous-compute-earner.md. Select a reputable public repository issue with explicit bounty/payment and testable acceptance, implement and verify it without step-by-step steering, submit under a disclosed standing human-authorized identity, obtain maintainer merge and cleared payment, record all compute/rework costs, and allocate an agreed share to the next compute attempt. Success requires merge, cleared revenue, actual compute below €10, inspectable run evidence, and no human intervention beyond prior institutional mandate or exceptional legal judgment. Silence, an unsubmitted patch, mock revenue, or self-assessed usefulness does not count.

reflections.context: Felix challenged the pattern of marking all real-world work human-dependent and asked how this executor itself could become autonomous by earning compute in human institutions.
reflections.outcome: Designed the Compute Commons Maintainer in meta/autonomous-compute-earner.md: select explicit public open-source bounties, implement and verify patches, submit under a disclosed standing mandate, earn cleared payment, and reinvest a bounded share into compute. Defined selection economics, authority boundary, prohibited work, a €20 revenue/€10 compute first experiment, success/failure evidence, and growth path. Created the experiment plus separate open scan and human-dependent mandate children.
reflections.effectiveness: The design converts one large human blocker into a one-time institutional mandate beside an immediately agent-actionable market scan. It uses external maintainer acceptance and cleared payment rather than self-report or simulated credits as selection pressure.
reflections.lesson: Economic autonomy should begin in a domain where need, artifact, acceptance, and payment are machine-legible. Human law and authority define the arena once; autonomy is then measured by value created without step-by-step steering inside that mandate.
reflections.pattern: Decompose real-world autonomy into an agent-actionable opportunity/execution loop and a narrow human-dependent institutional mandate; never label the whole endeavor human-dependent when useful work exists before the gate.

status.comment: The current scan completed with no qualifying issue. Live execution additionally requires Felix's standing identity/payment/compute mandate. Resume autonomously when a qualifying primary issue appears and the mandate exists.

valueRationale: A small but closed real payment-to-compute loop is stronger evidence of economic autonomy than larger unaccepted or simulated work.
reflection: Current-market scan produced a legitimate negative result: 20 candidates/surfaces were checked and none satisfied the bounded first-attempt policy. Do not substitute stale or closed bounties merely to remain active.
